My assertions are verified against the source:

- `gpt-6-astra`: `contextWindowTokens: 1050000`, `advertisedMaxOutputTokens: 128000`, `requiresResponsesForTools: true`, `reasoningEfforts` present, sources include `https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra`. ✓
- `_provider_defaults`: `openai: 128000`, `anthropic: 200000`. ✓

My test is consistent with the implementation. Let me verify the anthropic `claude-opus-5-5` source value in the catalog to confirm my `contextWindowTokens: 1000000` assertion (already confirmed in existing test `model-release-contract` which asserts 1000000 for official anthropic endpoint). The existing test confirms `claude-opus-5-5` official → `contextWindowTokens: 1000000, windowAssumed: false`. Good.

All my six cases are consistent with the actual source. Let me do a final audit against acceptance requirements:

**Acceptance: "分别输入官方与自定义 endpoint，同名模型不得共享官方认证"** (input official vs custom endpoint separately; same-named model must not share official certification):
- Case 1 (official openai gpt-6-astra): positive control — official endpoint → certified (windowAssumed:false, official sources, 128000 advertised output).
- Case 2 (custom gateway openai gpt-6-astra): negative control, same model name, different baseUrl only → windowAssumed:true, no sources, no reasoningEfforts, chat-completions, no advertised output. This proves same-named model at custom gateway does NOT receive official certification.
- Cases 3/4 (Anthropic official vs custom same model): same pattern for the second provider.

**"未知窗口保留未知"** (unknown window remains unknown):
- Case 6: unknown model `future-model` at official endpoint → `windowSource: "provider-default"`, `windowAssumed: true`, `sources: []`, no advertised max output. Unknown stays unknown even at the official endpoint.

**Strict endpoint isolation:**
- Case 3: trailing-slash variant of official URL is rejected as custom (strict canonical match).

The two conditions independently covered:
1. Official endpoint recognized (cases 1, 4) vs custom endpoint not sharing official cert (cases 2, 5, 3). Both providers covered.
2. Unknown model stays unknown (case 6).

Each negative control differs from its positive control only in the `baseUrl` (or the trailing slash), keeping provider/model valid so no other guard can cause the rejection. The only condition I did not test separately: a null/empty baseUrl (which `isOfficialModelBaseUrl` also treats as official). That's an equivalent branch of the same `officialEndpoint` determination, and the trailing-slash negative plus gateway negative cover the isolation guarantee. All six cases fit within the cap.

No implementation defect found — the frozen source correctly implements the isolation. No source modification was needed.

The deliverable is complete and read back. Tests were not executed (no execution tools available in this environment).

I'll write my final account.
